key_insight: The paper shows that a unified AI framework for liquid electrolyte design can be extended and reused effectively, with stronger robustness as data scales and better transfer across different chemical systems. It also demonstrates improved multiscale performance compared with baseline approaches.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of designing liquid electrolytes with AI models that are not only accurate, but also reusable, extensible, and reliable across different compositions and systems.
method: Extended an integrated modelling framework for liquid electrolyte design to test reusability and extensibility.
Evaluated how training data size and composition influence model robustness and generalization.
Benchmarked cross-system transferability and multiscale prediction performance against baseline methods.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this study provides evidence that unified modelling frameworks can generalize beyond a single task or dataset when carefully evaluated and extended. It offers practical guidance on how dataset scale and composition affect robustness, which is useful for building transferable scientific ML systems.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing the integrated electrolyte design framework and its extensions
A comparison chart of baseline vs. proposed framework performance across different systems
A robustness plot illustrating the effect of data size and composition on accuracy
An icon-based multiscale graphic linking molecular, formulation, and system-level prediction
paper_title: Reusability report: Exploring the utility and extensibility of an integrated modelling framework for liquid electrolyte design
paper_authors: Genming Lai, Juntao Zhao, Zekai Liu, Ruiqi Zhang, Hanming Li
